style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">If the Company stops participating in some of its multi-employer pension plans, the Company may be required to pay those plans an amount based on its allocable share of the unfunded vested benefits of the plan, referred to as a withdrawal liability.</span></td></tr></table><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company&#8217;s participation in multi-employer plans is outlined in the following tables.  The EIN / Pension Plan Number column provides the Employer Identification Number (&#8220;EIN&#8221;) and the three-digit pension plan number.  The most recent Pension Protection Act Zone Status available in 2021 and 2020 is for the plan&#8217;s year-end at December&#160;31, 2020 and December&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">31, 2019, respectively.  Among other factors, generally, plans in the red zone are less than </span>65 percent funded, plans in the yellow zone are less than 80 percent funded and plans in the green zone are at least 80<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> percent funded.  The FIP/RP Status Pending / Implemented Column indicates plans for which a funding improvement plan (&#8220;FIP&#8221;) or a rehabilitation plan (&#8220;RP&#8221;) is either pending or has been implemented.  Unless otherwise noted, the information for these tables was obtained from the Forms 5500 filed for each plan&#8217;s year-end at December&#160;31, 2020 and December&#160;31, 2019. The multi-employer contributions listed in the table below are the Company&#8217;s multi-employer contributions made in fiscal years 2021, 2020 and 2019.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New <td class="text"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"><tr><td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">16.</b></p></td><td style="padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">DISPOSAL OF BUSINESS</b></p></td></tr></table><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">On March 13, 2019, the Company completed the sale of its You Technology business to Inmar for total consideration of $565, including $396 of cash and $64 of preferred equity received upon closing. The Company is also entitled to receive other cash payments of $105 over <span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">five years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">. The transaction includes a long-term service agreement for Inmar to provide the Company digital coupon services. The sale resulted in a gain of $70, $52 net of tax, which is included in &#8220;Gain on sale of businesses&#8221; in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. The Company recorded the fair value of the long-term service agreement of $358 in &#8220;Other current liabilities&#8221; and &#8220;Other long-term liabilities&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets and such amount is being recorded as sales over the </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_i0m9h1ryMkmO-35T_uqogw;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;">10-year</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> agreement.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">On April 26, 2019, the Company completed the sale of its Turkey Hill Dairy business to an affiliate of Peak Rock Capital for total proceeds of $225. The sale resulted in a gain of $106, $80 net of tax, which is included in &#8220;Gain on sale of businesses&#8221; in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">In the third quarter of 2019, as a result of a portfolio review, the Company decided to divest its interest in Lucky&#8217;s Market. The Company recognized an impairment charge of $238 in the third quarter of 2019, which is included in OG&amp;A in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. The impairment charge consists of property, plant and equipment of $200, which includes $40 of finance lease assets; goodwill of $19; operating lease assets of $11; and other charges of $8. The amount of the impairment charge attributable to The Kroger Co. is $131, $100 net of tax, with the remaining amount attributable to the minority interest.  Subsequently, the decision was made by Lucky&#8217;s Market to file for bankruptcy in January 2020, which led the Company to fully write off the value of its investment and deconsolidate Lucky&#8217;s Market from the consolidated financial statements.  This resulted in an additional non-cash charge of $174, $125 net of tax, in the fourth quarter of 2019, which is included in OG&amp;A in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.  The amount of the total 2019 charge attributable to The Kroger Co. is $305, $225 net of tax.  The Company maintains liabilities associated with certain property related guarantees that will result in the Company making payments to settle these over time.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure related to a disposal group. Includes, but is not limited to, a discontinued operation, disposal classified as held-for-sale or disposed of by means other than sale or disposal of an individually significant component.</p></div>

This amendment allows companies to reclassify stranded tax effects resulting from the Tax Act from accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) to retained earnings. The Company adopted ASU 2018-02 on <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_astmen5wP0ui_p7XcoB0Tg;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">February 3, 2019</span></span>, which resulted in a decrease to AOCI and an increase to accumulated earnings of $146, primarily related to deferred taxes previously recorded for pension and other postretirement benefits and cash flow hedges.&#160; The adoption of this standard did not have an effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated results of operations or cash flows.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In August 2018, the FASB issued ASU 2018-15, &#8220;Intangibles &#8211; Goodwill and Other &#8211; Internal-Use Software: Customer&#8217;s Accounting for Implementation Costs Incurred in a Cloud Computing Arrangement That Is a Service Contract.&#8221; Under the new standard, implementation costs related to a cloud computing arrangement will be deferred or expensed as incurred, in accordance with the existing internal-use software guidance for similar costs. The new standard also prescribes the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow classification of the capitalized implementation costs and related amortization expense. The Company adopted this guidance on a prospective basis in the first quarter of 2020.  Capitalized implementation costs of </span>$151, net of accumulated amortization of $15, and $81, net of accumulated amortization of $2<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">, are included in &#8220;Other assets&#8221; in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets as of January 29, 2022 and January 30, 2021, respectively.  The corresponding cash flows related to these arrangements are included in &#8220;Net cash provided by operating activities&#8221; in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="text"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"><tr><td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">18.</b></p></td><td style="padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">RECENTLY ISSUED ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</b></p></td></tr></table><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">In March 2020, the FASB issued ASU 2020-04, &#8220;Reference Rate Reform (Topic 848): Facilitation of the Effects of Reference Rate Reform on Financial Reporting.&#8221; This standard provides optional expedients and exceptions for applying GAAP to certain contract modifications and hedging relationships that reference LIBOR or other reference rates expected to be discontinued. This guidance is effective upon issuance and can be applied through December 31, 2022. The Company may elect to apply the amendments for contract modifications by Topic or Industry Subtopic as of any date from the beginning of an interim period that includes or is subsequent to March 12, 2020. The adoption of the standard is not expected to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Operations, Consolidated Balance Sheets or Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AccountingPoliciesAbstract', window );"><strong>ACCOUNTING POLICIES</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_DescriptionOfBusinessBasisOfPresentationAndPrinciplesOfConsolidationPolicyTextBlock', window );">Description of Business, Basis of Presentation and Principles of Consolidation</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Description of Business, Basis of Presentation and Principles of Consolidation</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Kroger Co. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was founded in 1883 and incorporated in 1902.&#160; As of January 29, 2022, the Company was one of the largest retailers in the world based on annual sales.&#160; The Company also manufactures and processes food for sale by its supermarkets and online.&#160; The accompanying financial statements include the consolidated accounts of the Company, its wholly-owned subsidiaries and other consolidated entities.  Intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Refer to Note 17 for a description of changes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for recently adopted accounting standards regarding the implementation costs of cloud computing arrangements.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_FiscalPeriod', window );">Fiscal Year</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Fiscal Year</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s fiscal year ends on the Saturday nearest January&#160;31.&#160; The last three fiscal years consist of the <span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">52</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">-week periods ended January 29, 2022, January 30, 2021 and February 1, 2020.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_UseOfEstimates', window );">Pervasiveness of Estimates</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Pervasiveness of Estimates</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities.  Disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of consolidated revenues and expenses during the reporting period is also required.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Cash, Temporary Cash Investments and Book Overdrafts</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Cash, Temporary Cash Investments and Book Overdrafts</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Cash and temporary cash investments represent store cash and short-term investments with original maturities of less than three months.  Book overdrafts are included in &#8220;Trade accounts payable&#8221; and &#8220;Accrued salaries and wages&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_DepositsInTransitPolicyTextBlock', window );">Deposits In-Transit</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Deposits In-Transit</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Deposits in-transit generally represent funds deposited to the Company&#8217;s bank accounts at the end of the year related to sales, a majority of which were paid for with debit cards, credit cards and checks, to which the Company does not have immediate access but settle within a few days of the sales transaction.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_InventoryPolicyTextBlock', window );">Inventories</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Inventories</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (principally on a last-in, first-out &#8220;LIFO&#8221; basis) or market.&#160; In total, approximately 91% of inventories in 2021 and 92% of inventories in 2020 were valued using the LIFO method.&#160; The remaining inventories, including substantially all fuel inventories, are stated at the lower of cost (on a FIFO basis) or net realizable value.  Replacement cost was higher than the carrying amount by $1,570 at January 29, 2022 and $1,373 at January 30, 2021.&#160; The Company follows the Link-Chain, Dollar-Value LIFO method for purposes of calculating its LIFO charge or credit.  During 2020, the Company had a LIFO liquidation primarily related to pharmacy inventory. The liquidated inventory was carried at lower costs prevailing in prior years as compared with current costs. The effect of this reduction in inventory decreased &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; by approximately $76, $58 net of tax. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The item-cost method of accounting to determine inventory cost before the LIFO adjustment is followed for substantially all store inventories at the Company&#8217;s supermarket divisions.&#160; This method involves counting each item in inventory, assigning costs to each of these items based on the actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts) of each item and recording the cost of items sold.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The item-cost method of accounting allows for more accurate reporting of periodic inventory balances and enables management to more precisely manage inventory.  In addition, substantially all of the Company&#8217;s inventory consists of finished goods and is recorded at actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts).</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company evaluates inventory shortages throughout the year based on actual physical counts in its facilities.  Allowances for inventory shortages are recorded based on the results of these counts to provide for estimated shortages as of the financial statement date.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock', window );">Property, Plant and Equipment</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Property, Plant and Equipment</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Property, plant and equipment are recorded at cost or, in the case of assets acquired in a business combination, at fair value.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> Depreciation and amortization expense, which includes the depreciation of assets recorded under finance leases, is computed principally using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of individual assets.  Buildings and land improvements are depreciated based on lives varying from </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">10</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> to </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">40 years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.&#160; All new purchases of store equipment are assigned lives varying from </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_X-ue0zcMoES33G1MHWSBeA;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;">three</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> to </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">nine years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.  Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the lease term to which they relate, which generally varies from </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_pEjYYRybK0SHgZWg1YLJRA;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;">four</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> to </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">25 years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">, or the useful life of the asset.&#160; Food production plant, fulfillment center and distribution center equipment is depreciated over lives varying from </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_e8ZEbH3wyUOjVns8b1MB7A;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;">three</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> to </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">15 years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.  Information technology assets are generally depreciated over </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_6cfunCFnQkSoDzJrQXEKdQ;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;">three</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> to </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">five years</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.&#160; Depreciation and amortization expense was $2,824 in 2021, $2,747 in 2020 and $2,649 in 2019.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Interest costs on significant projects constructed for the Company&#8217;s own use are capitalized as part of the costs of the newly constructed facilities.&#160; Upon retirement or disposal of assets, the cost and related accumulated depreciation and amortization are removed from the balance sheet and any gain or loss is reflected in net earnings.  Refer to Note 3 for further information regarding the Company&#8217;s property, plant and equipment.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock', window );">Leases</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Leases</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company leases certain store real estate, warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, office space and equipment.  The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception.  Finance and operating lease assets and liabilities are recognized at the lease commencement date.  Finance and operating lease liabilities represent the present value of minimum lease payments not yet paid. Operating lease assets represent the right to use an underlying asset and are based upon the operating lease liabilities adjusted for prepayments, lease incentives and impairment, if any. To determine the present value of lease payments, the Company estimates an incremental borrowing rate which represents the rate used for a secured borrowing of a similar term as the lease.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Lease terms generally range from 10 to 20 years with options to renew for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_qIdEWpWZvECbP1B32RjXaQ;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">varying</span></span> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_Gc4W2e16zk2JCeL42ZnUsQ;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">terms</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> at the Company&#8217;s sole discretion. The lease term includes the initial contractual term as well as any options to extend the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise that option. Leases with an initial term of 12 months or less are not recorded on the balance sheet.  Certain leases include escalation clauses or payment of executory costs such as property taxes, utilities or insurance and maintenance.  Operating lease payments are charged on a straight-line basis to rent expense over the lease term and finance lease payments are charged to interest expense and depreciation and amortization expense over the lease term.  Assets under finance leases are amortized in accordance with the Company&#8217;s normal depreciation policy for owned assets or over the lease term, if shorter.  The Company&#8217;s lease agreements do not contain any residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.  For additional information on leases, see Note 9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy', window );">Goodwill</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Goodwill</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company reviews goodwill for impairment during the fourth quarter of each year, or earlier upon the occurrence of a triggering event.  The Company performs reviews of each of its operating divisions and other consolidated entities (collectively, &#8220;reporting units&#8221;) that have goodwill balances.  Generally, fair value is determined using a market multiple model, or discounted projected future cash flows, and is compared to the carrying value of a reporting unit for purposes of identifying potential impairment.  Projected future cash flows are based on management&#8217;s knowledge of the current operating environment and expectations for the future.  Goodwill impairment is recognized for any excess of the reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value over its fair value, not to exceed the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit.  Results of the goodwill impairment reviews performed during 2021, 2020 and 2019 are summarized in Note 2.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company monitors the carrying value of long-lived assets for potential impairment each quarter based on whether certain triggering events have occurred.&#160; These events include current period losses combined with a history of losses or a projection of continuing losses or a significant decrease in the market value of an asset.&#160; When a triggering event occurs, an impairment calculation is performed, comparing projected undiscounted future cash flows, utilizing current cash flow information and expected growth rates related to specific stores, to the carrying value for those stores.  If the Company identifies impairment for long-lived assets to be held and used, the Company compares the assets&#8217; current carrying value to the assets&#8217; fair value.  Fair value is based on current market values or discounted future cash flows.  The Company records impairment when the carrying value exceeds fair market value.  With respect to owned property and equipment held for disposal, the value of the property and equipment is adjusted to reflect recoverable values based on previous efforts to dispose of similar assets and current economic conditions.&#160; Impairment is recognized for the excess of the carrying value over the estimated fair market value, reduced by estimated direct costs of disposal.  The Company recorded asset impairments totaling $64, $70 and $120 in 2021, 2020 and 2019, respectively.  The decrease in the 2021 and 2020 impairment charges, compared to 2019, was the result of 35 planned store closures in 2020 recognized in 2019.  Costs to reduce the carrying value of long-lived assets for each of the years presented have been included in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as Operating, general and administrative (&#8220;OG&amp;A&#8221;) expense.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_AccountsPayableFinancingArrangementPolicyTextBlock', window );">Accounts Payable Financing Arrangement</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Accounts Payable Financing Arrangement</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company has an agreement with a third party to provide an&#160;accounts payable tracking&#160;system<span style="background:#ffffff;"> which facilitates participating suppliers&#8217; ability to finance payment obligations from the Company with designated third-party financial institutions.&#160;&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;background:#ffffff;">Participating suppliers may, at their sole discretion, make offers to finance one or more payment obligations of the Company prior to their scheduled due dates at a discounted price to participating financial institutions.  The Company&#8217;s obligations to its suppliers, including amounts due and scheduled payment dates, are not affected by suppliers&#8217; decisions to finance amounts under this arrangement.  These obligations are included in &#8220;Other current liabilities&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</span></p><span></span>

<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_ContingentConsiderationPolicyPolicyTextBlock', window );">Contingent Consideration</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Contingent Consideration</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s Home Chef business combination involves potential payment of future consideration that is contingent upon the achievement of certain performance milestones. The Company recorded contingent consideration at fair value at the date of acquisition based on the consideration expected to be transferred, estimated as the probability-weighted future cash flows, discounted back to present value using a discount rate determined in accordance with accepted valuation methods.&#160; The liability for contingent consideration is remeasured to fair value at each reporting period using Level 3 inputs, and the change in fair value, including accretion for the passage of time, is recognized in earnings until the contingency is resolved.  In 2021 and 2020, adjustments to increase the contingent consideration liability as of year-end were recorded for $66 and $189, respectively, in OG&amp;A expense. In 2019, an adjustment to decrease the contingent consideration liability as of year-end 2019 was recorded for ($69) in OG&amp;A expense. </p><span></span>

<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_StoreClosingAndOtherExpenseAllowancesPolicyTextBlock', window );">Store Closing Costs</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Store Closing Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company regularly evaluates the performance of its stores and periodically closes those stores that are underperforming.&#160; Related liabilities arise, such as severance, contractual obligations and other accruals associated with store closings.&#160; The Company records a liability for costs associated with an exit or disposal activity when the liability is incurred, usually in the period the store closes.&#160; Adjustments to closed store liabilities primarily relate to actual exit costs differing from original estimates. Adjustments are made for changes in estimates in the period in which the change becomes known.&#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Owned stores held for disposal are reduced to their estimated net realizable value. Costs to reduce the carrying values of property, plant, equipment and operating lease assets are accounted for in accordance with the Company&#8217;s policy on impairment of long-lived assets.&#160; Inventory write-downs, if any, in connection with store closings, are classified in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221;. Costs to transfer inventory and equipment from closed stores are expensed as incurred.&#160; </p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_PensionAndOtherPostretirementPlansPolicy', window );">Benefit Plans and Multi-Employer Pension Plans</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Benefit Plans and Multi-Employer Pension Plans</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company recognizes the funded status of its retirement plans on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.  Actuarial gains or losses, prior service costs or credits and transition obligations that have not yet been recognized as part of net periodic benefit cost are required to be recorded as a component of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (&#8220;AOCI&#8221;).  The Company has elected to measure defined benefit plan assets and obligations as of January 31, which is the&#160;</span><span style="background:#ffffff;">month-end</span>&#160;that is closest to its fiscal year-ends, which were January 29, 2022 for fiscal 2021 and January 30, 2021 for fiscal 2020.&#160;&#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The determination of the obligation and expense for company-sponsored pension plans and other post-retirement benefits is dependent on the selection of assumptions used by actuaries and the Company in calculating those amounts.&#160; Those assumptions are described in Note 14 and include, among others, the discount rate, the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets, mortality and the rates of increase in compensation and health care costs.&#160; Actual results that differ from the assumptions are accumulated and amortized over future periods and, therefore, generally affect the recognized expense and recorded obligation in future periods.&#160; While the Company believes that the assumptions are appropriate, significant differences in actual experience or significant changes in assumptions may materially affect the pension and other post-retirement obligations and future expense.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company also participates in various multi-employer plans for substantially all union employees.&#160; Pension expense for these plans is recognized as contributions are funded or when commitments are probable and reasonably estimable, in accordance with GAAP.  Refer to Note 15 for additional information regarding the Company&#8217;s participation in these various multi-employer pension plans.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company administers and makes contributions to the employee 401(k)&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">retirement savings accounts.  Contributions to the employee 401(k)&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">retirement savings accounts are expensed when contributed or over the service period in the case of automatic contributions.  Refer to Note 14 for additional information regarding the Company&#8217;s benefit plans.</span></p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Share Based Compensation</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes compensation expense for all share-based payments granted under fair value recognition provisions. The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense, net of an estimated forfeiture rate, over the requisite service period of the award based on the fair value at the date of the grant.&#160; The Company grants options for common shares (&#8220;stock options&#8221;) to employees under various plans at an option price equal to the fair market value of the stock option at the date of grant.&#160; Stock options typically expire 10 years from the date of grant. Stock options vest between <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_yEnYtVr1RkGhg5ISKftFMg;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">one</span></span> and five years from the date of grant.&#160; In addition to stock options, the Company awards restricted stock to employees and nonemployee directors under various plans. The restrictions on these awards generally lapse between <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_jwneQ6Bc40S6P-U71mZUJw;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">one</span></span> and five years from the date of the awards. The Company determines the fair value for restricted stock awards in an amount equal to the fair market value of the underlying shares on the grant date of the award.</p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Uncertain Tax Positions</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company reviews the tax positions taken or expected to be taken on tax returns to determine whether and to what extent a benefit can be recognized in its consolidated financial statements. <td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">Sales</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14.35pt;"><span style="margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">The Company recognizes revenues from the</span> retail <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> products, net of sales taxes,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">at</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the point</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">of</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;">sale.  Pharmacy sales</span> are<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> recorded when the </span>product is<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>provided <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;"> customer.  Digital channel originated sales are recognized either upon pickup in store or upon delivery to the customer.  </span>Amounts billed to a customer related to shipping and delivery represent revenues earned for the goods provided and are classified as sales.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> When shipping is discounted, it is recorded as an adjustment to sales.  </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Discounts provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to customers</span> by<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> the Company</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">at</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the time</span> of <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">including</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">those</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in connection with</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">loyalty</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cards,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">are recognized as </span>a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">reduction</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in sales</span> as <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the products </span>are<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> sold.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Discounts provided </span>by<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> vendors, usually in</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">form</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> coupons, are</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">not recognized </span>as a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">reduction</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sales provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> coupons</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>are <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">redeemable</span> at <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">any retailer that</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">accepts</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">coupons.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">The</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">records </span>a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">receivable </span>from<span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>the vendor<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>for the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> difference</span> in <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sales price</span> and <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cash received.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.5pt;"> </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">For merchandise sold in one of the Company&#8217;s stores or online, tender is accepted at the point of sale.  The Company acts as principal in certain vendor arrangements where the purchase and sale of inventory are virtually simultaneous. The Company records revenue and related costs on a gross basis for these arrangements.&#160; For pharmacy sales, collection of third-party receivables is typically expected within </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">three months</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> or less from the time of purchase.  The third-party receivables from pharmacy sales are recorded in Receivables in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets and were $774 as of January 29, 2022 and $672 as of January 30, 2021.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sells</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">its</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">own gift</span> cards<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>gift <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">certificates (collectively &#8220;gift cards&#8221;).</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.4pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Rather, it records </span>a<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> deferred revenue </span>liability equal to <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">amount</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> received.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span>A <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale</span> is <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">then</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognized when</span> the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> gift</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cards</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">are</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">redeemed</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to purchase</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company&#8217;s</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;">products.  The Company&#8217;s gift cards do not expire.  While gift cards are generally redeemed within </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">12 months</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">, some are never fully redeemed. The</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognizes gift card</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">breakage under the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">proportional</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">method,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">where</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognition</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">of breakage income</span> is based<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>upon <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the historical</span> run-off<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>rate<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> unredeemed gift cards.</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">  The Company&#8217;s gift card deferred revenue liability was $185 as of January 29, 2022 and $160 as of January 30, 2021.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt 5.3pt 0pt 0pt;"><i style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in-store</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">health</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">clinics, digital</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">coupon</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">services</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">and</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"> other </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">online sales not included in the categories above.</span></td></tr></table><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:2.09pt 0pt 0pt 6.35pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_MerchandiseCostsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Merchandise Costs</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Merchandise Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations includes product costs, net of discounts and allowances; advertising costs (see separate discussion below); inbound freight charges; warehousing costs, including receiving and inspection costs; transportation costs; and food production and operational costs.&#160; Warehousing, transportation and manufacturing management salaries are also included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item; however, purchasing management salaries and administration costs are included in the OG&amp;A line item along with most of the Company&#8217;s other managerial and administrative costs.&#160; Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company&#8217;s digital offerings originating from non-retail store locations are included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item.  Rent expense and depreciation and amortization expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Warehousing and transportation costs include distribution center direct wages, transportation direct wages, repairs and maintenance, utilities, inbound freight and, where applicable, third-party warehouse management fees.&#160; These costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company believes the classification of costs included in merchandise costs could vary widely throughout the industry.&#160; The Company&#8217;s approach is to include in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item the direct, net costs of acquiring products and making them available to customers.&#160; The Company believes this approach most accurately presents the actual costs of products sold.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes all vendor allowances as a reduction in merchandise costs when the related product is sold.&#160; When possible, vendor allowances are applied to the related product cost by item and, therefore, reduce the carrying value of inventory by item.&#160; When the items are sold, the vendor allowance is recognized.&#160; When it is not possible, due to systems constraints, to allocate vendor allowances to the product by item, vendor allowances are recognized as a reduction in merchandise costs based on inventory turns and, therefore, recognized as the product is sold.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Advertising Costs</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Advertising Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s advertising costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred and are included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160; The Company&#8217;s advertising costs totaled $984 in 2021, $888 in 2020 and $854 in 2019.&#160; The Company does not record vendor allowances for co-operative advertising as a reduction of advertising expense.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesPolicyTextBlock', window );">Operating, General and Administrative Expenses</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Operating, General and Administrative Expenses</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">OG&amp;A expenses consist primarily of employee-related costs such as wages, healthcare benefit costs, retirement plan costs, utilities, and credit card fees. Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company's digital offerings originating from retail store locations, including third-party delivery fees, are included in the &#8220;OG&amp;A&#8221; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations.  Rent expense, depreciation and amortization expense and interest expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_ConsolidatedStatementsOfCashFlowsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">For purposes of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, the Company considers all highly liquid debt instruments purchased with an original maturity of three months or less to be temporary cash investments.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock', window );">Segments</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Segments</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company operates supermarkets, multi-department stores and fulfillment centers throughout the United States.  The Company&#8217;s retail operations, which represent 97</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">% of the Company&#8217;s consolidated sales, are its only reportable segment.  The Company aggregates its operating divisions into one</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> reportable segment due to the operating divisions having similar economic characteristics with similar long-term financial performance.  In addition, the Company&#8217;s operating divisions offer customers similar products, have similar distribution methods, operate in similar regulatory environments, purchase the majority of the merchandise for retail sale from similar (and in many cases identical) vendors on a coordinated basis from a centralized location, serve similar types of customers, and are allocated capital from a centralized location.  Operating divisions are organized primarily on a geographical basis so that the operating division management team can be responsive to local needs of the operating division and can execute company strategic plans and initiatives throughout the locations in their operating division. This geographical separation is the primary differentiation between these retail operating divisions.  The geographical basis of organization reflects how the business is managed and how the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, who acts as the Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker, assesses performance internally.  All of the Company&#8217;s operations are domestic.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Disclosure of accounting policy for determining an entity's fiscal year or other fiscal period. This disclosure may include identification of the fiscal period end-date, the length of the fiscal period, any reporting period lag between the entity and its subsidiaries, or equity investees. If a reporting lag exists, the closing date of the entity having a different period end is generally noted, along with an explanation of the necessity for using different closing dates. Any intervening events that materially affect the entity's financial position or results of operations are generally also disclosed.</p></div>

This accounting policy may address (1) the types of plans sponsored by the entity, and the benefits provided by each plan (2) groups that participate in (or are covered by) each plan (3) how plan assets, liabilities and expenses are measured, including the use of any actuaries and (4) significant assumptions used by the entity to value plan assets and liabilities and how such assumptions are derived.</p></div>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Accumulated change in equity from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources, net of tax effect, at period end. Excludes Net Income (Loss), and accumulated changes in equity from transactions resulting from investments by owners and distributions to owners. Includes foreign currency translation items, certain pension adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on certain investments in debt and equity securities, other than temporary impairment (OTTI) losses related to factors other than credit losses on available-for-sale and held-to-maturity debt securities that an entity does not intend to sell and it is not more likely than not that the entity will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis, as well as changes in the fair value of derivatives related to the effective portion of a designated cash flow hedge.</p></div>
