The Company acts as principal in certain vendor arrangements where the purchase and sale of inventory are virtually simultaneous. The Company records revenue and related costs on a gross basis for these arrangements.&#160; For pharmacy sales, collection of third-party receivables is typically expected within &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;three months&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; or less from the time of purchase.  The third-party receivables from pharmacy sales are recorded in Receivables in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets and were $774 as of January 29, 2022 and $672 as of January 30, 2021.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt;Gift Cards and Gift Certificates&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:2.3pt;margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 5.3pt 0pt 0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;The&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Company&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;does&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;not&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;recognize&lt;/span&gt; revenue&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; when&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;it&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;sells&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;its&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;own gift&lt;/span&gt; cards&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;and&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;gift &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;certificates (collectively &#x201c;gift cards&#x201d;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:2.4pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Rather, it records &lt;/span&gt;a&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; deferred revenue &lt;/span&gt;liability equal to &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt;amount&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; received.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;A &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;sale&lt;/span&gt; is &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;then&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;recognized when&lt;/span&gt; the&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; gift&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;cards&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;are&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt;redeemed&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;to purchase&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;the&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Company&#x2019;s&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;products.  The Company&#x2019;s gift cards do not expire.  While gift cards are generally redeemed within &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;12 months&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;, some are never fully redeemed. The&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Company&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;recognizes gift card&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;breakage under the&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;proportional&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt;method,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;where&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;recognition&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;of breakage income&lt;/span&gt; is based&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;upon &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;the historical&lt;/span&gt; run-off&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;rate&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;of&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; unredeemed gift cards.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;  The Company&#x2019;s gift card deferred revenue liability was $185 as of January 29, 2022 and $160 as of January 30, 2021.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New     <kr:MerchandiseCostsPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="Duration_1_31_2021_To_1_29_2022_RZeFCZSJIUShRsFbtTBwgA"
      id="Tb_pL9vflHoSU-5LT3c-_Bq9A">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Merchandise Costs&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations includes product costs, net of discounts and allowances; advertising costs (see separate discussion below); inbound freight charges; warehousing costs, including receiving and inspection costs; transportation costs; and food production and operational costs.&#160; Warehousing, transportation and manufacturing management salaries are also included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item; however, purchasing management salaries and administration costs are included in the OG&amp;amp;A line item along with most of the Company&#x2019;s other managerial and administrative costs.&#160; Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company&#x2019;s digital offerings originating from non-retail store locations are included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item.  Rent expense and depreciation and amortization expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Warehousing and transportation costs include distribution center direct wages, transportation direct wages, repairs and maintenance, utilities, inbound freight and, where applicable, third-party warehouse management fees.&#160; These costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company believes the classification of costs included in merchandise costs could vary widely throughout the industry.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s approach is to include in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item the direct, net costs of acquiring products and making them available to customers.&#160; The Company believes this approach most accurately presents the actual costs of products sold.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes all vendor allowances as a reduction in merchandise costs when the related product is sold.&#160; When possible, vendor allowances are applied to the related product cost by item and, therefore, reduce the carrying value of inventory by item.&#160; When the items are sold, the vendor allowance is recognized.&#160; When it is not possible, due to systems constraints, to allocate vendor allowances to the product by item, vendor allowances are recognized as a reduction in merchandise costs based on inventory turns and, therefore, recognized as the product is sold.&lt;/p&gt;</kr:MerchandiseCostsPolicyTextBlock>

      contextRef="Duration_1_31_2021_To_1_29_2022_RZeFCZSJIUShRsFbtTBwgA"
      id="Tb_JXJIvnP92kCjPF5lY4pOKQ">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Segments&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company operates supermarkets, multi-department stores and fulfillment centers throughout the United States.  The Company&#x2019;s retail operations, which represent 97&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;% of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated sales, are its only reportable segment.  The Company aggregates its operating divisions into one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; reportable segment due to the operating divisions having similar economic characteristics with similar long-term financial performance.  In addition, the Company&#x2019;s operating divisions offer customers similar products, have similar distribution methods, operate in similar regulatory environments, purchase the majority of the merchandise for retail sale from similar (and in many cases identical) vendors on a coordinated basis from a centralized location, serve similar types of customers, and are allocated capital from a centralized location.  Operating divisions are organized primarily on a geographical basis so that the operating division management team can be responsive to local needs of the operating division and can execute company strategic plans and initiatives throughout the locations in their operating division. This geographical separation is the primary differentiation between these retail operating divisions.  The geographical basis of organization reflects how the business is managed and how the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer, who acts as the Company&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker, assesses performance internally.  All of the Company&#x2019;s operations are domestic.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock>

Further, the Company has recorded a valuation allowance against certain deferred tax assets resulting from its state credits.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company regularly reviews all deferred tax assets on a tax filer and jurisdictional basis to estimate whether these assets are more likely than not to be realized based on all available evidence.  This evidence includes historical taxable income, projected future taxable income, the expected timing of the reversal of existing temporary differences and the implementation of tax planning strategies.  Projected future taxable income is based on expected results and assumptions as to the jurisdiction in which the income will be earned.  The expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences is based on current tax law and the Company&#x2019;s tax methods of accounting.  Unless deferred tax assets are more likely than not to be realized, a valuation allowance is established to reduce the carrying value of the deferred tax asset until such time that realization becomes more likely than not.  Increases and decreases in these valuation allowances are included in "Income tax expense" in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. As of January 29, 2022, January 30, 2021 and February 1, 2020 the total valuation allowance was $72, $53 and $55, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New These measures include deferring the due dates of tax payments and other changes to income and non-income-based tax laws. As permitted under the CARES Act, the Company deferred the remittance of the employer portion of the social security tax.  The social security tax provision requires that the deferred employment tax be paid over &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;two years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;, with half of the amount required to be paid by December 31, 2021 and the other half to be paid by December 31, 2022. During 2020, the Company deferred the employer portion of social security tax of $622. Of the total, $311 was paid during 2021 and $311 is included in &#x201c;Other current liabilities&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock>

In connection with the senior note issuances, the Company also terminated forward-starting interest rate swap agreements with an aggregate notional amount of &lt;/span&gt;$450&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; due in fiscal year 2030. These forward-starting interest rate swap agreements were hedging the variability in future benchmark interest payments attributable to changing interest rates on the forecasted issuance of fixed-rate debt issued during the fourth quarter of 2020.  Since these forward-starting interest rate swap agreements were classified as cash flow hedges, the unamortized loss of &lt;/span&gt;$41, $31&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; net of tax, has been deferred in Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss and will continue to amortize to earnings as the interest payments are made.  The Company repaid &lt;/span&gt;$700 of senior notes bearing an interest rate of 3.30%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; with proceeds from the senior notes issuances.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;On March 18, 2020, the Company proactively borrowed $1,000 under the revolving credit facility. This was a precautionary measure in order to preserve financial flexibility, reduce reliance on the commercial paper market and maintain liquidity in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. During 2020, the Company fully repaid the $1,000 borrowed under the revolving credit facility and the entire $1,150 in outstanding commercial paper obligations, as of February 1, 2020, using cash generated by operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration-line:line-through;text-decoration-style:solid;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;On July 6, 2021, the Company entered into an amended, extended and restated &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;$2,750&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt; unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#x201c;Credit Agreement&#x201d;), with a termination date of July 6, 2026, unless extended as permitted under the Credit Agreement. The Company has the ability to increase the size of the Credit Agreement by up to an additional &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;$1,250&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;, subject to certain conditions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest, at the Company&#x2019;s option, at either (i) LIBOR plus a market spread, based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating or (ii) the base rate, defined as the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5%, (b) Bank of America prime rate, and (c) one-month LIBOR plus 1.0%, plus a market rate spread based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  The Company will also pay a Commitment Fee based on its Public Debt Rating and Letter of Credit fees equal to a market rate spread based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating.  &#x201c;Public Debt Rating&#x201d; means, as of any date, the rating that has been most recently announced by either S&amp;amp;P or Moody&#x2019;s, as the case may be, for any class of non-credit enhanced long-term senior unsecured debt issued by the Company.  The Credit Agreement includes fallback language related to the transition from LIBOR to alternative reference rates.  The Company does not expect a significant change to its cost of debt as a result of the transition from LIBOR to an alternative reference rate.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Credit Agreement contains a covenant, which, among other things, requires the maintenance of a Leverage Ratio of not greater than 3.50&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;:1.00.  The Company may repay the Credit Agreement in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty.  The Credit Agreement is not guaranteed by the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As of January 29, 2022, and January 30, 2021, the Company had no commercial paper borrowings and no borrowings under the Credit Agreement.&lt;span style="color:#ff0000;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#ff0000;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As of January 29, 2022, the Company had outstanding letters of credit in the amount of $363, of which $2 reduces funds available under the Credit Agreement. As of January 30, 2021, the Company had outstanding letters of credit in the amount of $381, of which $2 reduces funds available under the Credit Agreement.&#160;The letters of credit are maintained primarily to support performance, payment, deposit or surety obligations of the Company.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span outstanding public debt is subject to early redemption at varying times and premiums, at the option of the Company.&#160; In addition, subject to certain conditions, some of the Company&#x2019;s publicly issued debt will be subject to redemption, in whole or in part, at the option of the holder upon the occurrence of a redemption event, upon not less than five days&#x2019; notice prior to the date of redemption, at a redemption price equal to the default amount, plus a specified premium.&#160; &#x201c;Redemption Event&#x201d; is defined in the indentures as the occurrence of (i)&#160;any person or group, together with any affiliate thereof, beneficially owning 50% or more of the voting power of the Company, (ii)&#160;any one person or group, or affiliate thereof, succeeding in having a majority of its nominees elected to the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors, in each case, without the consent of a majority of the continuing directors of the Company or (iii)&#160;both a change of control and a below investment grade rating.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span       id="Tb_JLKzigxJN0aokZQsKAOuIg">&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;6.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;DERIVATIVE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;GAAP requires that derivatives be carried at fair value on the balance sheet and provides for hedge accounting when certain conditions are met.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s derivative financial instruments are recognized on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160; Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments designated as &#x201c;cash flow&#x201d; hedges, to the extent the hedges are highly effective, are recorded in other comprehensive income, net of tax effects.  Ineffective portions of cash flow hedges, if any, are recognized in current period earnings.&#160; Other comprehensive income or loss is reclassified into current period earnings when the hedged transaction affects earnings.&#160; Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments designated as &#x201c;fair value&#x201d; hedges, along with corresponding changes in the fair values of the hedged assets or liabilities, are recorded in current period earnings.  Ineffective portions of fair value hedges, if any, are recognized in current period earnings.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company assesses, both at the inception of the hedge and on an ongoing basis, whether derivatives used as hedging instruments are highly effective in offsetting the changes in the fair value or cash flow of the hedged items. &#160;If it is determined that a derivative is not highly effective as a hedge or ceases to be highly effective, the Company discontinues hedge accounting prospectively.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Interest Rate Risk Management&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company is exposed to market risk from fluctuations in interest rates. The Company manages its exposure to interest rate fluctuations through the use of a commercial paper program, interest rate swaps (fair value hedges) and forward-starting interest rate swaps (cash flow hedges). The Company&#x2019;s current program relative to interest rate protection contemplates hedging the exposure to changes in the fair value of fixed-rate debt attributable to changes in interest rates. To do this, the Company uses the following guidelines: (i) use average daily outstanding borrowings to determine annual debt amounts subject to interest rate exposure, (ii) limit the average annual amount subject to interest rate reset and the amount of floating rate debt to a combined total amount that represents 25% of the carrying value of the Company&#x2019;s debt portfolio or less, (iii) include no leveraged products, and (iv) hedge without regard to profit motive or sensitivity to current mark-to-market status.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company reviews compliance with these guidelines annually with the Financial Policy Committee of the Board of Directors.&#160; These guidelines may change as the Company&#x2019;s needs dictate.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration-color:#000000;text-decoration-line:underline;text-decoration-style:solid;"&gt;Fair Value Interest Rate Swaps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New January 30, 2021.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p terminated nine forward-starting interest rate swaps with maturity dates of January 2021 with an aggregate notional amount totaling $450&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  These forward-starting interest rate swap agreements were hedging the variability in future benchmark interest payments attributable to changing interest rates on the forecasted issuance of fixed-rate debt issued during the fourth quarter of 2020.  Since these forward-starting interest rate swap agreements were classified as cash flow hedges, the unamortized loss of $41, $31&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; net of tax, has been deferred in AOCI and will be amortized to earnings as the interest payments are made. indirectly observable;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p primarily used in the impairment analysis of goodwill, other intangible assets, long-lived assets and in the valuation of store lease exit costs.  The Company reviews goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment annually, during the fourth quarter of each fiscal year, and as circumstances indicate the possibility of impairment.  See Note 2 for further discussion related to the Company&#x2019;s carrying value of goodwill.  Long-lived assets and store lease exit costs were measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis using Level 3 inputs as defined in the fair value hierarchy.  See Note 1 for further discussion of the Company&#x2019;s policies for impairments of long-lived assets and valuation of store lease exit costs.  In 2021, long-lived assets with a carrying amount of &lt;/span&gt;$74 were written down to their fair value of $10, resulting in an impairment charge of $64&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  In 2020, long-lived assets with a carrying amount of &lt;/span&gt;$72 were written down to their fair value of $2, resulting in an impairment charge of $70.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight:bold;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Fair Value of Other Financial Instruments&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Current and Long-term Debt&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The fair value of the Company&#x2019;s long-term debt, including current maturities, was estimated based on the quoted market prices for the same or similar issues adjusted for illiquidity based on available market evidence.  If quoted market prices were not available, the fair value was based upon the net present value of the future cash flow using the forward interest rate yield curve in effect at respective year-ends.  At January 29, 2022, the fair value of total debt excluding obligation under finance leases was &lt;/span&gt;$13,189 compared to a carrying value of $11,745&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  At January 30, 2021, the fair value of total debt excluding obligation under finance leases was &lt;/span&gt;$14,680 compared to a carrying value of $12,410. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Contingent Consideration&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;As a result of the Home Chef merger, the Company recognized a contingent liability of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;$91&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;background:#ffffff;"&gt; on the acquisition date.  The contingent consideration was measured using unobservable (Level 3) inputs and was included in &lt;/span&gt;&#x201c;Other long-term liabilities&#x201d; within the Consolidated Balance Sheet&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;.&#160;The Company estimated the fair value of the earnout liability by applying a &lt;/span&gt;Monte-Carlo simulation method&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt; using the Company&#x2019;s projection of future operating results for both the online and offline businesses related to the Home Chef merger and the estimated probability of achievement of the earnout target metrics.&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;The Monte-Carlo simulation is a generally accepted statistical technique used to generate a defined number of valuation paths in order to develop a reasonable estimate of the fair value of the earnout liability.&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The liability is remeasured to fair value using the Monte-Carlo simulation method at each reporting period, and the change in fair value, including accretion for the passage of time, is recognized in net earnings until the contingency is resolved.  In 2020, the Company amended the contingent consideration agreement including the performance milestones to align with the Company&#x2019;s current business strategies.  In 2021 and 2020, the Company recorded adjustments to increase the contingent consideration liability for &lt;/span&gt;$66 and $189, respectively, in OG&amp;amp;A.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and Temporary Cash Investments, Store Deposits In-Transit, Receivables, Prepaid and Other Current Assets, Trade Accounts Payable, Accrued Salaries and Wages and Other Current Liabilities&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The carrying amounts of these items approximated fair value due to their short term nature.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Assets&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The equity investment in Ocado Group plc is measured at fair value through net earnings. The fair value of all shares owned, which is measured using Level 1 inputs, was $987 and $1,808 as of January 29, 2022 and January 30, 2021, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets. The unrealized gain (loss) for this Level 1 investment was approximately ($821) and $1,032 for 2021 and 2020, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;(Loss) Gain on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company held other equity investments without a readily determinable fair value. These investments are measured initially at cost and remeasured for observable price changes to fair value through net earnings. The value of these investments was $309 and $189 as of January 29, 2022 and January 30, 2021, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; During 2020, certain of these investments with a carrying value of $87 were remeasured to their fair value of $160, resulting in an unrealized gain of $73.&#160; The gain was measured using Level 3 inputs and is included in &#x201c;(Loss) Gain on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160; There were no observable price changes or impairments for these investments during 2021, and as such, they are excluded from the fair value measurements table above for January 29, 2022.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New In 2020, the Company entered into sale leaseback transactions related to seven properties, which resulted in total proceeds of $78. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;On May 17, 2018, the Company entered into a Partnership Framework Agreement with Ocado International Holdings Limited and Ocado Group plc (&#x201c;Ocado&#x201d;), which has since been amended. Under this agreement, Ocado will partner exclusively with the Company in the U.S., enhancing the Company&#x2019;s digital and robotics capabilities in its distribution networks. The Company opened its first three Kroger Delivery customer fulfillment centers in Monroe, Ohio, Groveland, Florida and Forest Park, Georgia. The Company determined the arrangement with Ocado contains a lease of the robotic equipment used to fulfill customer orders. As a result, the Company established a finance lease when each facility began fulfilling orders to customers and used its &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_I44x6UCmLEamhen0HQWRgQ;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;10-year&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; incremental borrowing rate to calculate the lease liability. The base term of each lease is &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;10 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; with options to renew at the Company&#x2019;s sole discretion. The Company elected to combine the lease and non-lease elements in the contract. As a result, it will account for all payments to Ocado as lease payments. In 2021, the Company recorded finance lease assets of $401 and finance lease liabilities of $372 related to these location openings.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</kr:LeaseDisclosureTextBlock>

    <us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock
      contextRef="Duration_1_31_2021_To_1_29_2022_RZeFCZSJIUShRsFbtTBwgA"
      id="Tb_txhS7pbTHkCs-kMe9Ip0gQ">&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;11.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes compensation expense for all share-based payments granted. The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense, net of an estimated forfeiture rate, over the requisite service period of the award based on the fair value at the date of the grant. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company grants options for common shares (&#x201c;stock options&#x201d;) to employees under various plans at an option price equal to the fair market value of the stock option at the date of grant. The Company accounts for stock options under the fair value recognition provisions. Stock options typically expire 10 years from the date of grant. Stock options vest between &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_06wqhb4G1UqgRcciqDDdXA;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and five years from the date of grant. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;In addition to the stock options described above, the Company awards restricted stock to employees and nonemployee directors under various plans. The restrictions on these awards generally lapse between &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_GcJ2Cpx3wkSChHYSJ_y92g;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and five years&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; from the date of the awards.  The Company determines the fair value for restricted stock awards in an amount equal to the fair market value of the underlying shares on the grant date of the award.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;At January 29, 2022, approximately 19 million common shares were available for future options or restricted stock grants under the 2011, 2014, and 2019 Long-Term Incentive Plans (the &#x201c;Plans&#x201d;). Options granted reduce the shares available under the Plans at a ratio of one&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; to one.  Restricted stock grants reduce the shares available under the Plans at a ratio of 2.83 to one.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Equity awards granted are based on the aggregate value of the award on the grant date. This can affect the number of shares granted in a given year as equity awards. Excess tax benefits related to equity awards are recognized in the provision for income taxes. Equity awards may be approved at one of four meetings of its Board of Directors occurring shortly after the Company&#x2019;s release of quarterly earnings. The 2021 primary grants were made in conjunction with the March and June meetings of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;All awards become immediately exercisable upon certain changes of control of the Company.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Stock Options&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The weighted-average grant date fair value of stock options granted during 2021, 2020 and 2019 was $8.54, $6.43 and $6.00&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;, respectively.  The fair value of each stock option grant was estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, based on the assumptions shown in the table below.  The Black-Scholes model utilizes accounting judgment and financial estimates, including the term option holders are expected to retain their stock options before exercising them, the volatility of the Company&#x2019;s share price over that expected term, the dividend yield over the term and the number of awards expected to be forfeited before they vest.  Using alternative assumptions in the calculation of fair value would produce fair values for stock option grants that could be different than those used to record stock-based compensation expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.  The increase in the fair value of the stock options granted during 2021, compared to 2020, resulted primarily from increases in the Company&#x2019;s share price and the weighted-average expected volatility.  The increase in the fair value of the stock options granted during 2020, compared to 2019, resulted primarily from increases in the Company&#x2019;s share price and the weighted-average expected volatility, partially offset by a decrease in the interest rate.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span &#x2014; The Company&#x2019;s workers&#x2019; compensation risks are self-insured in most states. In addition, other workers&#x2019; compensation risks and certain levels of insured general liability risks are based on retrospective premium plans, deductible plans, and self-insured retention plans.&#160; The liability for workers&#x2019; compensation risks is accounted for on a present value basis.&#160; Actual claim settlements and expenses incident thereto may differ from the provisions for loss.&#160; Property risks have been underwritten by a subsidiary and are all reinsured with unrelated insurance companies.&#160; Operating divisions and subsidiaries have paid premiums, and the insurance subsidiary has provided loss allowances, based upon actuarially determined estimates.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Litigation &#x2014; &lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;Various claims and lawsuits arising in the normal course of business, including personal injury, contract disputes, employment discrimination, wage and hour and other regulatory claims are pending against the Company.  Some of these suits purport or have been determined to be class actions and/or seek substantial damages.  Although it is not possible at this time to evaluate the merits of all of these claims and lawsuits, nor their likelihood of success, the Company is of the belief that any resulting liability will not have a material effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company continually evaluates its exposure to loss contingencies arising from pending or threatened litigation and believes it has made provisions where it is reasonably possible to estimate and when an adverse outcome is probable.  Nonetheless, assessing and predicting the outcomes of these matters involves substantial uncertainties.  Management currently believes that the aggregate range of loss for the Company&#x2019;s exposure is not material to the Company.  It remains possible that despite management&#x2019;s current belief, material differences in actual outcomes or changes in management&#x2019;s evaluation or predictions could arise that could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;On February 9, 2022, a putative shareholder filed a derivative action in the Court of Common Pleas, Hamilton County, Ohio against certain current and former directors of The Kroger Co. and The Kroger Co., as a nominal defendant, alleging among other things, that the defendants breached their fiduciary duties in connection with the data incident involving the Company&#x2019;s former third party secure file transfer vendor, Accellion.&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company is one of dozens of companies that have been named in various lawsuits alleging that defendants contributed to create a public nuisance through the distribution and dispensing of opioids. &#160;&#160;At present, the Company is named in a significant number of lawsuits pending in various state courts as well as in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio, where over&#160;2,000&#160;cases have been consolidated as Multi-District Litigation ("MDL") pursuant to 28 U.S.C. &#xa7;1407 in a case entitled &lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;In re National Prescription Opiate Litigation&lt;/i&gt;.&#160;&#160; Once discovery is completed, those cases will be remanded to the originating federal court for trial. The Company only funds obligations under the Qualified Plans.  Funding for the company-sponsored pension plans is based on a review of the specific requirements and on evaluation of the assets and liabilities of each plan.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;In addition to providing pension benefits, the Company provides certain health care benefits for retired employees. style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;white-space:nowrap;width:3.41%;margin:0pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s discount rate assumptions were intended to reflect the rates at which the pension benefits could be effectively settled.&#160; They take into account the timing and amount of benefits that would be available under the plans.  The Company&#x2019;s policy is to match the plan&#x2019;s cash flows to that of a hypothetical bond portfolio whose cash flow from coupons and maturities match the plan&#x2019;s projected benefit cash flows.  The discount rates are the single rates that produce the same present value of cash flows.  The selection of the 3.17% and 3.01&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;% discount rates as of year-end 2021 for pension and other benefits, respectively, represents the hypothetical bond portfolio using bonds with an AA or better rating constructed with the assistance of an outside consultant.  A 100 basis point increase in the discount rate would decrease the projected pension benefit obligation as of January 29, 2022, by approximately $316.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s 2021 assumed pension plan investment return rate was 5.50% compared to 5.50% in 2020 and 6.00&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;% in 2019.  The value of all investments in the company-sponsored defined benefit pension plans during the calendar year ended December 31, 2021, net of investment management fees and expenses, increased 5.9% and for fiscal year 2021 investments increased 4.2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;%.  Historically, the Company&#x2019;s pension plans&#x2019; average rate of return was 8.2% for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_7W5WO8o85kCWNGxjVdeoyw;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;10&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; calendar years ended December 31, 2021, net of all investment management fees and expenses.  For the past &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;20 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;, the Company&#x2019;s pension plans&#x2019; average annual rate of return has been 7.8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;%.  To determine the expected rate of return on pension plan assets held by the Company, the Company considers current and forecasted plan asset allocations as well as historical and forecasted rates of return on various asset categories.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company calculates its expected return on plan assets by using the market-related value of plan assets.  The market-related value of plan assets is determined by adjusting the actual fair value of plan assets for gains or losses on plan assets.  Gains or losses represent the difference between actual and expected returns on plan investments for each plan year.  Gains or losses on plan assets are recognized evenly over a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;five-year&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; period.  Using a different method to calculate the market-related value of plan assets would provide a different expected return on plan assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The pension benefit unfunded status decreased in 2021, compared to 2020, due primarily to an increase in discount rates, reducing the benefit obligation.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The following objectives, policies and strategies are set by the Retirement Benefit Plan Management Committee (the &#x201c;Committee&#x201d;).&#160; The primary objectives include holding and investing the assets and distributing benefits to participants and beneficiaries of the pension plans.&#160; Investment objectives have been established based on a comprehensive review of the capital markets and each underlying plan&#x2019;s current and projected financial requirements.&#160; The time horizon of the investment objectives is long-term in nature and plan assets are managed on a going-concern basis.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p for a purpose or in a manner not specifically authorized is prohibited, unless approved in advance by the Committee.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Company&#x2019;s LDI strategy. An LDI strategy focuses on maintaining a close to fully-funded status over the long-term with minimal funded status risk.  This is achieved by investing more of the plan assets in fixed income instruments to more closely match the duration of the plan liability.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company did not make any contributions to its company-sponsored pension plans in 2021, and the Company is not required to make any contributions to these plans in 2022.  If the Company does make any contributions in 2022, the Company expects these contributions will decrease its required contributions in future years.  Among other things, investment performance of plan assets, the interest rates required to be used to calculate the pension obligations, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;future changes in legislation, will determine the amounts of any contributions.  The Company expects 2022 net periodic benefit costs for company-sponsored pension plans to be approximately ($38).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Assumed health care cost trend rates have a significant effect on the amounts reported for the health care plans.&#160; The Company used a 5.30% initial health care cost trend rate, which is assumed to decrease on a linear basis to a 4.50% ultimate health care cost trend rate in 2037, to determine its expense.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p The assets&#x2019; fair value measurement level above is based on the lowest level of any input that is significant to the fair value measurement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The following is a description of the valuation methods used for the Qualified Plans&#x2019; assets measured at fair value in the above tables:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Cash and cash equivalents: The carrying value approximates fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Corporate Stocks: The fair values of these securities are based on observable market quotations for identical assets and are valued at the closing price reported on the active market on which the individual securities are traded.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Corporate Bonds: The fair values of these securities are primarily based on observable market quotations for similar bonds, valued at the closing price reported on the active market on which the individual securities are traded. When such quoted prices are not available, the bonds are valued using a discounted cash flow approach using current yields on similar instruments of issuers with similar credit ratings, including adjustments for certain risks that may not be observable, such as credit and liquidity risks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;U.S. Government Securities: Certain U.S. Government securities are valued at the closing price reported in the active market in which the security is traded. Other U.S. government securities are valued based on yields currently available on comparable securities of issuers with similar credit ratings. When quoted prices are not available for similar securities, the security is valued under a discounted cash flow approach that maximizes observable inputs, such as current yields of similar instruments, but includes adjustments for certain risks that may not be observable, such as credit and liquidity risks. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Mutual Funds: The fair values of these securities are based on observable market quotations for identical assets and are valued at the closing price reported on the active market on which the individual securities are traded.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;Collective Trusts: The collective trust funds are public investment vehicles valued using a Net Asset Value (NAV) provided by the manager of each fund.  These assets have been valued using NAV as a practical expedient.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Hedge Funds: The Hedge funds classified as Level 3 include investments that are not readily tradeable and have valuations that are not based on readily observable data inputs. The fair value of these assets is estimated based on information provided by the fund managers or the general partners. Therefore, these assets are classified as Level 3.&#160; Certain other hedge funds are private investment vehicles valued using a NAV provided by the manager of each fund.&#160; These assets have been valued using NAV as a practical expedient.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;Private Equity: Private Equity investments are valued based on the fair value of the underlying securities within the fund, which include investments both traded on an active market and not traded on an active market. For those investments that are traded on an active market, the values are based on the closing price reported on the active market on which those individual securities are traded.  For investments not traded on an active market, or for which a quoted price is not publicly available, a variety of unobservable valuation methodologies, including discounted cash flow, market multiple and cost valuation approaches, are employed by the fund manager to value investments.  Fair values of all investments are adjusted annually, if necessary, based on audits of the private equity fund financial statements; such adjustments are reflected in the fair value of the plan&#x2019;s assets. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:18pt;"/&gt;&lt;td style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&#x25cf;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;Real Estate: Real estate investments include investments in real estate funds managed by a fund manager.  These investments are valued using a variety of unobservable valuation methodologies, including discounted cash flow, market multiple and cost valuation approaches.&#160; The valuations for these investments are not based on readily observable inputs and are classified as Level 3 investments.&#160; Certain other real estate investments are valued using a NAV provided by the manager of each fund.&#160; These assets have been valued using NAV as a practical expedient.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The methods described above may produce a fair value calculation that may not be indicative of net realizable value or reflective of future fair values.  Furthermore, while the Company believes its valuation methods are appropriate and consistent with other market participants, the use of different methodologies or assumptions to determine the fair value of certain financial instruments could result in a different fair value measurement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company contributed and expensed $289, $294 and $264 to employee 401(k)&#160;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;retirement savings accounts in 2021, 2020 and 2019, respectively.  The 401(k)&#160;retirement savings account plans provide to eligible employees both matching contributions and automatic contributions from the Company based on participant contributions, compensation as defined by the plan and length of service.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt;In 2019, the Company approved and implemented a plan to reorganize certain portions of its division management structure.&#160; This reorganization increased operational effectiveness and reduced overhead costs while maintaining a high quality customer experience.&#160; The Company recorded a charge for severance and related benefits of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt;$80&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt;$61&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt; net of tax, in 2019, which is included in the OG&amp;amp;A caption within the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;&lt;/span&gt;Of the total charge, $42 was unpaid as of February 1, 2020 and was included in Other Current Liabilities within the Consolidated Balance Sheet and the remaining balance was paid in 2020.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRoman';visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsDisclosureTextBlock>

These multi-employer pension plans provide retirement benefits to participants based on their service to contributing employers.  The benefits are paid from assets held in trust for that purpose.  Trustees are appointed in equal number by employers and unions.  The trustees typically are responsible for determining the level of benefits to be provided to participants as well as for such matters as the investment of the assets and the administration of the plans.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company recognizes expense in connection with these plans as contributions are funded or when commitments are probable and reasonably estimable, in accordance with GAAP.  &lt;/span&gt;The Company made cash contributions to these plans of $1,109 in 2021, $619 in 2020 and $461 in 2019. The increase in 2021, compared to 2020, is due to the contractual payments made in 2021 related to our commitments established for certain ratification agreements.&#160; The increase in 2020, compared to 2019, is due to incremental contributions we made in 2020 to multi-employer pension plans, helping stabilize future associate benefits.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company continues to evaluate and address potential exposure to under-funded multi-employer pension plans as it relates to the Company&#x2019;s associates who are beneficiaries of these plans.&#160; These under-fundings are not a liability of the Company.  When an opportunity arises that is economically feasible and beneficial to the Company and its associates, the Company may negotiate the restructuring of under-funded multi-employer pension plan obligations to help stabilize associates&#x2019; future benefits and become the fiduciary of the restructured multi-employer pension plan.  The commitments from these restructurings do not change the Company&#x2019;s debt profile as it relates to its credit rating since these off balance sheet commitments are typically considered in the Company&#x2019;s investment grade debt rating.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company is currently designated as the named fiduciary of the United Food and Commercial Workers (&#x201c;UFCW&#x201d;) Consolidated Pension Plan and the International Brotherhood of Teamsters (&#x201c;IBT&#x201d;) Consolidated Pension Fund and has sole investment authority over these assets.&#160;Due to opportunities arising, the Company has restructured certain multi-employer pension plans.       contextRef="Duration_1_31_2021_To_1_29_2022_RZeFCZSJIUShRsFbtTBwgA"
      id="Tb_6_cGf9jZ70ayWHfd7twu9g">&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;17.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;RECENTLY ADOPTED ACCOUNTING STANDARDS&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;In February 2018, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201c;FASB&#x201d;) issued ASU 2018-02, "Income Statement&#x2014;Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income." This amendment allows companies to reclassify stranded tax effects resulting from the Tax Act from accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) to retained earnings. The Company adopted ASU 2018-02 on &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_astmen5wP0ui_p7XcoB0Tg;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;February 3, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, which resulted in a decrease to AOCI and an increase to accumulated earnings of $146, primarily related to deferred taxes previously recorded for pension and other postretirement benefits and cash flow hedges.&#160; The adoption of this standard did not have an effect on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated results of operations or cash flows.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;In August 2018, the FASB issued ASU 2018-15, &#x201c;Intangibles &#x2013; Goodwill and Other &#x2013; Internal-Use Software: Customer&#x2019;s Accounting for Implementation Costs Incurred in a Cloud Computing Arrangement That Is a Service Contract.&#x201d; Under the new standard, implementation costs related to a cloud computing arrangement will be deferred or expensed as incurred, in accordance with the existing internal-use software guidance for similar costs. The new standard also prescribes the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow classification of the capitalized implementation costs and related amortization expense. The Company adopted this guidance on a prospective basis in the first quarter of 2020.  Capitalized implementation costs of &lt;/span&gt;$151, net of accumulated amortization of $15, and $81, net of accumulated amortization of $2&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;, are included in &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets as of January 29, 2022 and January 30, 2021, respectively.  The corresponding cash flows related to these arrangements are included in &#x201c;Net cash provided by operating activities&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsAndChangesInAccountingPrinciplesTextBlock>
